A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research and provide readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Content can be matched despite relocated references, renumbering, and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, human preferences, component ablations, and an appendix simulation of 2D distribution matching.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds diversity measurements, CLIP-space distributional evaluations, and component comparisons.

M1.justification: The GRPO procedure, composite rewards, EMA LOO-FID formulation, adaptive entropy mechanism, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. The revised entropy target is an experimental hyperparameter-setting change, rather than a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet class-conditional generation and the same 2D line-distribution simulation. Additional metrics and controls use retained coverage; removing selected qualitative examples does not remove the underlying ImageNet or no-CFG scenarios.

E2.justification: AR-GRPO, VA-π, pretrained models, and MLE remain the external or standard baselines. v2 adds batch-only LOO-FID and fixed/scheduled entropy comparator variants in Tables 16–17. MANIQA already participates in v1 Table 4; its new citation does not establish a new baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds DreamSim/LPIPS evaluation using eight samples per ImageNet class, CLIP-space distribution metrics, and new component controls. It also replaces v1 Appendix C's fixed entropy target of 0.78 with a target 10% above each pretrained model's entropy in Appendix D. This is a reported setting revision; the PDFs do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands validation of the central diversity-preserving mechanisms: Appendix G isolates EMA versus minibatch statistics, Appendix H tests adaptive versus fixed/scheduled entropy, and Table 5 directly examines intra-class diversity. Appendix E adds a complementary feature-space analysis. These address questions beyond v1's existing reward, covariance, KL, and entropy-coefficient ablations.

E5.justification: v2 introduces two-sided binomial significance tests, excluding ties, for the unchanged human-study counts. It reports significance for three comparisons and p = 0.34 for CFG realism. Neither version supplies repeated-training-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Existing benchmark scores and human-study counts are retained. New results include DreamSim/LPIPS of 0.53/0.73 for ours versus 0.49/0.72 for AR-GRPO, CLIP-space scores, and FIDs of 4.06 for batch LOO-FID and 4.10/4.12 for scheduled/fixed entropy versus 3.83 for the retained method. These are additional comparisons, not improved v1-to-v2 scores. The Bobsled/Golf Ball examples are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations and derivations in Section 3 and Appendices B–C are retained. No new theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical correction is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims concerning distribution-level rewards, adaptive regularization, quality and diversity improvements, and avoiding CFG's doubled inference cost.

C2.justification: v2 qualifies the human-preference interpretation using significance tests and adds interpretations connecting EMA, adaptive entropy, and intra-class diversity to coverage preservation. Appendix E newly argues for semantic distributional alignment, although Table 15 shows decreased CLIP-Recall for LlamaGen-B. The stated limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds Table 14 with model-specific architecture dimensions, token grids, batch sizes, and optimization epochs. It also adds a project/source-code link and states that implementation and pretrained models are public. v1 already contains substantial pseudocode, hyperparameters, and computational-cost details.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for DreamSim, Pick-a-Pic/PickScore, MANIQA, and LPIPS. The positioning relative to diffusion alignment and concurrent autoregressive RL methods, including the distribution-level novelty claim, remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises the introductory post-training paragraph and human-study discussion, removes a duplicated distribution-reward analysis paragraph, and updates affiliations and acknowledgments. References move after the appendix, which gains several subsections; most existing prose and narrative order are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 5 and 14–17, expands the presentation of the retained MLE table, and removes v1 Figure 6. Remaining qualitative panels are retained with relocation, renumbering, and caption edits, including an expanded Monitor/Wine Bottle caption. The overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: The new EMA and entropy controls, intra-class diversity measurements, and human-study significance tests strengthen support for existing claims. Added settings and resource-access information also aid reproducibility. These gains outweigh limited weaknesses: Table 14 is not fully reconciled with the shared-hyperparameter description, and Appendix E's broad coverage-preservation wording overlooks LlamaGen-B's reduced CLIP-Recall in Table 15.
